method: Two-round batch elicitation. A fresh assistant instance with no access to expected answers read the round-one packet (mixed tool catalog and 24 requests) and wrote its tool calls as JSON. The harness executed those calls over HTTP against local fixture servers and wrote a round-two packet holding the real tool results. The same instance then wrote its replies to the users. Fixed rules graded the saved transcript.
limits: One trial per case. No repeated runs, so there is no variance estimate.
All 24 requests were presented in one batch per round. The assistant was told to treat each as a separate conversation but could see the others.
Tool calls were written as JSON and executed by the harness. No production MCP client and no client tool-calling loop was involved.
The assistant knew it was taking part in an evaluation.

The assistant was instructed to read only the packet file. The harness cannot technically prevent it from reading other files; the session reported two tool calls in round one and three in round two, consistent with one read and one write per round.
Fixture data: the bundled snapshot at a fixed clock. The weather source is unreachable by design, so weather context is unavailable.
Answer checks are regular-expression heuristics. They are not a judgment of answer quality.
Three size tiers of one model family from one vendor.
